report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of daedalus/eval/harness.py: arms aggregate, Tier2 runner, provider detection, baseline load/snapshot/write. Claims mostly kept; one uncheckable.
risks: run_arms:142 | medium | _arms_aggregate reads r['id'] but _correctness_task_row and _task_error_row may omit 'id'? (uncheckable in this chunk) | check those row constructors' key sets
detect_provider:184 | medium | OLLAMA_MODEL env may name a model absent from /api/tags; code silently falls back to first model, ignoring user intent | test with OLLAMA_MODEL set to a non-listed name
_ask:205 | medium | chat_completion called with force_json=False but system prompt asks for strict context-only; no verification that answer adheres | inspect _openai_compat.chat_completion behavior

run_tier2:224 | medium | whole_true_tokens_cache computes full text via _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars=None) but that function may still impose its own cap or fail on huge repos | read _whole_repo_text implementation
write_baseline:271 | high | open(...,'w') is not atomic; a crash mid-write corrupts baseline.json, and the docstring promises deterministic diff | use atomic replace or temp file

snapshot_baseline:255 | medium | if run_tier1 returns 'error' key but also 'recall' (e.g. partial), the comprehension includes it? guard is 'error' not in t and not focus_withheld; if both error and recall present, it snapshots recall | verify run_tier1 row shape
run_arms:144 | low | per_task rows for correctness tasks may lack fields like 'tokens_A' that _arms_aggregate expects; aggregation could KeyError | check _correctness_task_row output

run_tier2:233 | medium | tasks without 'question' are silently skipped, not counted as errored or skipped; n_tasks may undercount and the skip is invisible | consider adding a 'skipped_no_question' counter

handoff.purpose: Arms aggregation, Tier2 LLM comparison, provider detection, and baseline load/snapshot/write.

symbols.name: _arms_aggregate
symbols.note: Aggregates per-task arms rows into summary counts and means.

symbols.name: run_arms
symbols.note: Runs deterministic A/B/C comparison over tasks, skipping correctness tasks and collecting per-provenance aggregates.

symbols.name: _score
symbols.note: Checks all expected substrings appear case-insensitively; returns success bool and fraction.

symbols.name: detect_provider
symbols.note: Probes local Ollama /api/tags; returns descriptor or None.

symbols.name: _ask
symbols.note: Single LLM turn; catches all exceptions and returns empty string.

symbols.name: run_tier2
symbols.note: Opt-in Tier2: compares distilled slice vs whole-repo-concat success and tokens; skips cleanly without provider.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH
symbols.note: Path to baseline.json next to this file.

symbols.name: load_baseline
symbols.note: Reads baseline.json or returns empty baseline if missing.

symbols.name: snapshot_baseline
symbols.note: Builds baseline structure from run_tier1 results; skips errored and focus-withheld tasks.

symbols.name: write_baseline
symbols.note: Writes baseline.json with deterministic formatting; explicit-only.

claims.text: Model-free (recall via _recall), offline, no LLM -- safe to run alongside Tier 1.
claims.why: run_arms only calls resolve_task_repo, cached_index, _repo_chunks, eval_task_arms, _correctness_task_row, _task_error_row; none invoke _ask or detect_provider; no network calls in this chunk.

claims.text: See eval_task_arms for what each arm measures and by_provenance for the (never-blended) per-provenance-tier breakdown.
claims.why: eval_task_arms and by_provenance are defined elsewhere in the file; this chunk only shows the call to _by_provenance(healthy, _arms_aggregate).

claims.text: Tie-inclusive on purpose: a strict '>' here silently counted a BM25 tie as an A win, contradicting the 'C>=A' column header (report.py) and this function's own docstring ('if C ties or beats A ... that is reported loudly, not smoothed over').
claims.why: Line 577 uses recall_c >= recall_a, inclusive of ties, so a tie yields c_beats_a=True.

claims.text: recall_A==1.0 on every current hand_reachable task makes a strict C win impossible, so with '>' the tie case ... was the ONLY case that could ever fire and it was being absorbed into 'no'.
claims.why: The claim about current task recall values depends on data outside this chunk; the code change itself (>=) is visible and kept.

claims.text: Success = every expected substring appears (case-insensitive). Also return the fraction present for a softer signal.
claims.why: Lines 181-185: low = answer.lower(); present counts substrings whose lowercased form is in low; success iff present == len(answer_contains).

claims.text: Only a local Ollama HTTP endpoint is probed (free, no key, no egress).
claims.why: Lines 190-197: host defaults to http://127.0.0.1:11434 (or OLLAMA_HOST), and the only network call is urllib.request.urlopen to that host's /api/tags. No external egress unless OLLAMA_HOST is set to a remote host, but the docstring says 'local' and the default is local.

claims.text: The probe is a 2s GET to /api/tags -- it does nothing unless Tier 2 is requested.
claims.why: timeout=2 is set on urlopen; detect_provider is only called from run_tier2 in this chunk (line 213), which is Tier 2.
Lines 204-209: the only call to chat_completion is wrapped in try/except Exception, and the except returns empty string.

claims.text: Opt-in Tier 2. Compares distilled-slice (A) vs whole-repo-concat (B) task success + tokens. Cleanly skipped (never crashes) when no provider is up.
claims.why: Lines 213-215: if detect_provider returns None, returns a skipped dict; no exception path visible. The comparison is implemented by _ask on ctx_a and ctx_b and _score.

claims.text: B's tokens were ALREADY measured with the real tokenizer before this change (count_tokens is exact whenever tiktoken is installed) -- that part was honest.
claims.why: count_tokens is imported from elsewhere; its exactness depends on tiktoken availability, not visible here.

claims.text: B is capped at cap_tokens * 4 chars before being measured, so tokens_B silently reflected a TRUNCATED text, not the real whole-repo size. tokens_B_true (added here) is the untruncated whole-repo token count, so a truncated B can never be mistaken for the real baseline.
claims.why: Lines 221: cap_chars = cap_tokens * 4; line 228: whole_cache[repo] = _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars); line 230: full_text, _ = _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars=None); line 231: whole_true_tokens_cache[repo] = count_tokens(full_text); lines 252-253 record tokens_B and tokens_B_true.

claims.text: Read baseline.json, or an empty baseline if it does not exist yet (a fresh repo checkout before the first --update-baseline run).
claims.why: Lines 243-246: if not os.path.exists(p) returns {'schema': 1, 'tasks': {}}; otherwise opens and json.load.

claims.text: Pure: build the baseline structure for the CURRENT recall of tasks (default TASKS). Does not touch disk -- see write_baseline.
claims.why: Lines 250-258: calls run_tier1 (no disk write visible), builds dict, returns; no file I/O in this function.

claims.text: Every task is snapshotted (including quarantine ones) so quarantine promotion is still comparable later; only PRIMARY tasks are ever gated (see run_gate).
claims.why: The docstring claims quarantine tasks are snapshotted, but the code only excludes errored and focus_withheld; it does not filter by tier. Whether quarantine tasks are included depends on run_tier1's per_task contents, which is not in this chunk. The gating behavior is in run_gate, not here.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (run_tier1) have no recall to snapshot and are skipped here -- they simply get no baseline entry, which makes them a 'new task' (not silently a pass) the next time run_gate sees them resolve successfully.
claims.why: Lines 256-258: comprehension includes only rows where 'error' not in t and not t.get('focus_withheld'); so errored rows are excluded.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file) are skipped for the same reason: there is no recall key to snapshot, and re-baselining a fence-refused task would silently launder 'never measured' into 'passing'.
claims.why: Lines 256-258: comprehension excludes rows with t.get('focus_withheld').

claims.text: EXPLICIT-ONLY baseline write. Never call this from an automatic code path -- a baseline that updates itself is not a ratchet, it is a no-op. Only the '--update-baseline' CLI flag (a human decision) should reach this.
claims.why: The docstring describes call-site policy; this chunk only contains the function definition. The function itself does not guard against automatic calls; it just writes.

claims.text: Returns the path written. Deterministic formatting (sorted keys) so the diff is meaningful in review.
claims.why: The function body is truncated at line 271; the return and the actual json.dump with sort_keys are not visible in this chunk.

observations.what: write_baseline writes directly with open(...,'w') without atomic write; a crash mid-write could corrupt baseline.json, and the docstring promises deterministic diff.
_arms_aggregate reads r['id'] but the rows from _correctness_task_row and _task_error_row may or may not include 'id'; if they don't, KeyError on aggregated sets.
detect_provider falls back to models[0] if OLLAMA_MODEL is set but not in the model list, silently ignoring the user's requested model.
run_tier2 skips tasks without 'question' silently, not counted in n_tasks or errored; undercounts and hides the skip.
whole_true_tokens_cache calls _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars=None) which may still impose its own cap or fail on huge repos; the docstring claims it is untruncated.

snapshot_baseline excludes rows with 'error' in t, but if a row has both 'error' and 'recall' (e.g., partial error), it would be excluded anyway; the guard is fine but the docstring says errored tasks 'have no recall' -- uncheckable if that's always true.
run_arms catches only (ValueError, OSError) around resolve_task_repo, cached_index, _repo_chunks; other exceptions (e.g., KeyError from task['repo']) would propagate and crash the whole run.
